abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary malignant brain tumor in adults, characterized by high invasiveness and poor prognosis. The knowledge of driver genes and prognostic markers predictive of poor outcomes in GBM is still limited. In the current article, we show that late endosomal/lysosomal adapter and MAPK and MTOR activator 5 (LAMTOR5) is a driver gene for GBM progression through transcriptionally activating the HOXC9/YTHDF2 positive feedback loop. LAMTOR5 is highly expressed in GBM, predicts poor prognosis in glioma patients and is essential for the growth, invasion, and tumorigenesis of GBM cells. Using a bioinformatics analysis approach based on multiple public datasets, we identified YTHDF2 as a downstream effector of LAMTOR5. LAMTOR5 promotes the expression of YTHDF2 through increasing its promoter activity by coactivating the transcription factor HOXC9. In turn, the LAMTOR5-upregulated YTHDF2 enhances the expression of HOXC9 through promoting the mRNA stability of HOXC9 in an m6A-dependent manner, forming a positive feedback loop in LAMTOR5-overexpressed GBM cells. Silencing YTHDF2 can abrogate the LAMTOR5-promoted proliferation and invasion of glioma cells both in vitro and in vivo. Thus, we conclude that LAMTOR5 is an oncogenic protein driving GBM progression via activating the HOXC9/YTHDF2 positive feedback loop. Our results offer new insights into the regulatory interplay between transcription and m6A modification of oncogenic proteins in GBM and provide a therapeutic target for GBM treatment.
